title: Summer work for his father and his family in Xenia
summary: He worked summers for his father's contracting business around Xenia, Springfield and Columbus; the storm that ruined the family house; his siblings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How old were you when you went to work for your father?
Hmm?
Did you go to work for your father, Jerry, when you were still in school?
Did I work for my father when?
Like, while you were still in school.
Well, when I got in high school, that's when I worked; in the summertime, you know. That was during that period.
During the holidays.
Well, no, not during the holidays. Just a summer job, you know. ...(?)... to contract houses -- to plaster and all that, you know: that's what I was going to be.
He had his own business, then.
Yes. He was his own...
And that was in Xenia.
Dickenson - 5
Partly Xenia and partly Springfield, partly Columbus.
I was thinking about you when they had that hurricane.

Yes. Well, it ruined our house there. We had to destroy it, because it was too rickety to stand. But it's a funny thing, too. I had just put this aluminum cover over it, and all of that money got messed away. It's all re-done now. It's tough to put it on the ...(? )...(? )...
Who was living there then?
Oh, just my niece was there...was living there then. I had just gone, just about a year before -- my sister was living at the time. She died in ...(? )...
Were you the youngest?
Yes. I'm the youngest living. There were two younger than me, but they died years ago. Two girls who were younger. But now I only have one brother living, and he's in the hospital... And that's that.
Your brother who was a musician, was he a musician when you were kids?
No. He had other activities to do.
How much difference was there between you?
The one that you've seen in the picture?
Yes.
